content_units: This plan is built for a full-time worker with   10.5 study hours/week  :   90 minutes Monday-Friday  ,   3 hours Saturday  ,   Sunday off  . It prioritizes your weak areas first—  subnetting and routing  —while keeping steady review so you retain the rest.
-   Sat:   longer lab/practice exam block + error review
Use a simple   Red / Yellow / Green tracker   for each exam domain:
-   Red:   cannot explain or solve without notes
-   Yellow:   mostly understand, still slow or inconsistent
-   Green:   can answer correctly and explain why
-   All domains at Yellow or Green
Week   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz

1   Week 1   Network fundamentals + OSI/TCP-IP + ports   Mon: models and traffic flow; Tue: devices/cabling basics; Wed: ports/protocols; Thu: topologies and common services; Fri: 25-question review; Sat: flashcards + mini quiz   Explain layers, common ports, and device roles from memory

2   Week 2   IP addressing + subnetting core   Mon: IPv4 structure/CIDR; Tue: subnet masks and host counts; Wed: subnetting drills; Thu: VLSM and practical questions; Fri: timed subnet quiz; Sat: 90-minute subnet workshop + corrections   Solve basic subnetting problems accurately and faster

3   Week 3   Routing, switching, VLANs, NAT, DHCP   Mon: routing concepts and metrics; Tue: static vs dynamic routing; Wed: switching, VLANs, trunks; Thu: NAT, DHCP, ARP; Fri: mixed quiz; Sat: diagram-based troubleshooting lab   Understand packet path, VLAN purpose, and routing behavior

4   Week 4   Wireless, network services, cloud, virtualization   Mon: Wi-Fi standards/channels/security; Tue: VPNs and remote access; Wed: DNS, NTP, SNMP, syslog; Thu: cloud and virtual networking; Fri: 30-question quiz; Sat: weak-topic review block   Recognize service roles and compare deployment models

5   Week 5   Network security   Mon: threats and attack types; Tue: hardening and segmentation; Wed: AAA, auth methods, certificates; Thu: firewalls, NAC, secure protocols; Fri: security quiz; Sat: scenario questions + notes cleanup   Match security controls to real network risks

6   Week 6   Operations, monitoring, documentation, troubleshooting method   Mon: monitoring tools and metrics; Tue: diagrams, configs, baselines; Wed: change management and DR concepts; Thu: troubleshooting methodology; Fri: mixed quiz; Sat: performance and log interpretation lab   Apply structured troubleshooting and operational best practices

7   Week 7   Full-domain reinforcement + practice exam focus   Mon: subnetting/routing review; Tue: security refresh; Wed: services/wireless refresh; Thu: troubleshooting refresh; Fri: light review; Sat: full practice exam + deep review   Identify remaining weak objectives and close gaps

8   Week 8   Final review and exam readiness   Mon: missed-question log review; Tue: subnetting speed drill; Wed: routing/services review; Thu: acronyms/ports/facts; Fri: light confidence review; Sat: final practice exam or half-length timed set   Enter exam week with stable scores and low-error weak areas
-   20 min:   practice questions or subnetting drills
-   15 min:   write 3-5 takeaways and update tracker
-   60 min:   labs, diagrams, or scenario questions
-   15 min:   error log update and next-week focus
Review Cadence That Fits a Work Schedule
-   Same day:   5-minute recap at end of session
-   Next day:   start by recalling yesterday’s key points
-   Friday:   review everything studied that week
-   Saturday:   cumulative review across current + prior weeks
-   End of Weeks 4, 7, 8:   bigger checkpoint using mixed questions
- At least   10-15 subnetting problems   until speed improves
Because you are already stronger in hardware troubleshooting, this plan delays heavy time on that area and spends early energy on the highest-friction concepts.
- Subnetting and routing improve with repetition, so they need   early placement and repeated returns
- Security and operations are easier once the network foundations are solid
- Troubleshooting becomes stronger when you already know how traffic and services should behave
Readiness Tracker You Can Use in One Page
Create a simple sheet with these columns:
At the end of each Saturday:
- Mark any topic below   70%   as   Red
- Carry forward the top   2 weakest topics   into next week’s Friday or Saturday review
